newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila call loan rates rise on weekend covering.
newsitem.headline: Manila call loan rates rise on weekend covering.

text.p: *Volume expands to 28.327 bln pesos from 17.594 bln

- Philippine interbank call loan rates jumped to an average of 12.8125 percent on Thursday from 11.15625 percent in the last trading day on Friday amid covering of six days of reserve positions, traders said.
Banks were last open on Friday but had to cover positions from that day until Wednesday.
Done rates moved between a high of 13.75 percent and a low of 11.25, with 28 borrowers and 37 lenders.
"It was a bit tight but not as tight as expected," a dealer from a foreign bank said.
Traders said borrowers in the market were mostly small banks, while big banks were lenders.
"Since the beginning, they (the big banks) were lending," a trader said, adding that these banks had prepared for the high demand for pesos since last week by borrowing heavily.
Near the end of the session, dealers said rates had gone down to around 11.75 percent, near the day-low of 11.25 percent.
Dealers said the rise in interest rates was viewed as temporary and will soon ease with the cut in reserve requirements.
Some 6.7 billion pesos will be released from the Central Bank as a one percentage-point cut in reserve requirements takes effect on Friday, January 3.
At the secondary market trading of T-bills, dealers said banks were buying more of the six months and one-year bills.
Banks were positioning ahead of an expected drop in interest rates due to the lower reserve requirements, a trader said.

According to a Reuter poll of six financial institutions, banks were quoting bid rates of 11.55 to 11.80 percent on three-month bills; 11.80 to 12.10 on six months; and 12.10 to 12.60 on one year bills.
